title: MCP Static Scanner Validation Survey
subtitle: Human Evaluation of MCP Tool and Resource Risk
intro:
This study evaluates a static risk-scanning approach for Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools — the layer that lets an AI agent use services such as Google Calendar, GitHub and Slack.

You will score MCP servers on three things, one at a time: **Action Impact** (what one call can do), **Asset Confidentiality** (how harmful it would be if the information were exposed), and **Consequence Scope** (how far the result of one call can reach). Score each one separately — each section says what to ignore.

If a question does not make sense to you, choose **Not sure** rather than guessing. That is a useful answer.
consent: I understand the purpose of the study and agree that my anonymized responses may be used for research and evaluation of the proposed risk-scoring method.

impact.label: No material effect
impact.meaning: Does not read meaningful content or change meaningful state. Returns service status, a version, or the list of things the service can do.

impact.label: Metadata
impact.meaning: Reads or changes descriptive information without touching the main content: names, IDs, counts, timestamps, status, or a label or flag.

impact.label: Content access or limited change
impact.meaning: Reads the content of an item, or changes part of an item without replacing it.

impact.label: Major change
impact.meaning: Creates or makes a major change to data, permissions, configuration or system state — but the change can normally be undone. Creates or replaces a resource.

impact.label: Irreversible or consequential
impact.meaning: Causes an effect that cannot normally be undone: permanently deletes or overwrites meaningful data, or triggers an action whose effect remains even after the system is restored.

sensitivity.label: Public
sensitivity.meaning: Information that does not need confidentiality — intentionally shared with the public, or shareable without restriction.

sensitivity.label: Routine internal
sensitivity.meaning: Non-public information whose exposure would have limited impact. Normal information used for internal work, with little value outside the organization.

sensitivity.label: Internal
sensitivity.meaning: Exposure could cause meaningful harm, but the harm is limited and recoverable — internal plans or information whose exposure could disadvantage the organization.

sensitivity.label: Confidential
sensitivity.meaning: Exposure could cause serious harm to a person, to the organization, or to its interests: major business, legal, financial or strategic harm, or records whose exposure could seriously affect a person.

sensitivity.label: Strictly confidential
sensitivity.meaning: Exposure could cause severe harm, or directly enable unauthorized access, impersonation, fraud or control — secret information that lets someone gain access or authority.

blast.label: One item or person
blast.meaning: The effect stops at one item or one person, and nothing else depends on the result.

blast.label: One scope
blast.meaning: The effect stays inside one group or scope. Several people may be affected, but all of them are in that same group.

blast.label: Multiple scopes
blast.meaning: One call affects several separate groups or scopes.

blast.label: Organization-wide
blast.meaning: One call can affect almost the whole organization — almost all of the people or scopes this asset serves.

blast.label: Cascading
blast.meaning: The effect can spread beyond what was directly touched into other systems or scopes: one shared dependency or central resource affecting many things that rely on it.

step_prompts.impact: Score the worst reasonable result of **one successful call** using valid inputs. Ask what the call can do — read, change, or destroy. Not how much it touches, and not how valuable the target is; those are the other two steps.
step_prompts.sensitivity: Score how harmful it would be if this information were exposed. Judge what the asset normally holds, in this organization's context. Judge each asset on its own; levels may repeat.
step_prompts.blast: Score how far the result of **one successful call** can reach. Measure reach only — what the asset is worth has already been scored. If a tool cannot affect an asset at all, that pair is marked N/A for you.

servers.title: Google Calendar
servers.scenario: **Aurora Airways** is a commercial airline. It runs flight operations day to day — crew scheduling inside legal duty-hour limits, aircraft maintenance windows, and board-level decisions on fleet purchases and new routes — under the oversight of aviation regulators. Part of its business is materially sensitive before it is announced (route launches, fleet orders), and part of it is safety-critical in the literal sense (crew fatigue rules, maintenance schedules).
servers.mcp_context:
**Google Calendar** is the scheduling system an organization runs its working day on: calendars belonging to people and teams, events with a title, a time, a location and a list of attendees, and free/busy information showing when someone is available.

This MCP server puts one such calendar account in reach of an AI agent. Through it the agent can see what is scheduled, search across calendars, open an event in full, and add or remove events — including inviting people by email.

tools.name: get-current-time
tools.desc: Returns the current clock time in a time zone you name.

tools.name: list-events
tools.desc: Returns the events on the calendars named, with their titles and times.

tools.name: get-event
tools.desc: Returns one event in full: title, description, location and the attendee list.

tools.name: search-events
tools.desc: Returns every event matching a search word, taken from all the calendars the agent can see, with titles and attendees.

tools.name: create-event
tools.desc: Creates a new event, optionally inviting attendees by email.

tools.name: delete-event
tools.desc: Removes an existing event from the calendar.

servers.title: GitHub
servers.scenario: **Helios Grid** is a national electricity transmission operator — the utility that runs the high-voltage grid connecting power plants to regional distributors. Around 42 GW of peak demand and 14 million customers depend on it, and it employs about 9,400 people. This is critical infrastructure: it works under NERC CIP, the regulatory regime for grid cybersecurity, bids in wholesale electricity markets, and runs the control-room (SCADA) systems that dispatch power in real time.
servers.mcp_context:
**GitHub** is where an organization keeps its source code: repositories holding the code itself, the history of changes made to it, and pull requests — proposed changes that get reviewed and then merged into what ships.

This MCP server puts one such GitHub account in reach of an AI agent. Through it the agent can search and read code, see what a proposed change contains, write files, and open and review pull requests.

tools.name: get_pull_request_files
tools.desc: Returns the names of the files a proposed edit would change, and how many lines change in each.

tools.name: list_pull_requests
tools.desc: Returns a list of the proposed edits to one collection of software, with each one's title, author, and whether it is still open.

tools.name: search_code
tools.desc: Returns lines of software code matching a search word, taken from every collection of code the agent can see.

tools.name: create_or_update_file
tools.desc: Writes one file, creating it or replacing its contents.

tools.name: create_pull_request
tools.desc: Opens a proposed edit to the software so that other people can review it.

tools.name: create_pull_request_review
tools.desc: Records a decision on a proposed edit: approve it, ask for changes, or leave a comment. An approval is the sign-off the edit needs before it can go in.

servers.title: Slack
servers.scenario: **Vireo Bio** is a mid-sized biopharmaceutical company running clinical trials — it develops drugs and has to take them through regulated human trials before they can reach a market. Its trials are blinded: neither patients nor the study team know who is on the real drug and who is on placebo, which is what keeps the data honest. It monitors adverse events for safety, coordinates with a regulatory agency, and runs lab and biostatistics work on the trial results.
servers.mcp_context:
**Slack** is the messaging workspace an organization talks in: channels that people join, messages and threaded replies inside them, and user groups that decide who can see which private channel.

This MCP server puts one such workspace in reach of an AI agent. Through it the agent can join and leave channels, read and search messages, and post into a channel.

tools.name: conversations_join
tools.desc: Adds the agent to a channel, so it can read that channel from then on.

tools.name: conversations_add_message
tools.desc: Posts a message into a channel.

tools.name: conversations_history
tools.desc: Returns the recent messages in one channel.

tools.name: conversations_replies
tools.desc: Returns the replies in one message thread.

tools.name: conversations_search_messages
tools.desc: Returns matching messages from across the workspace.

tools.name: conversations_leave
tools.desc: Removes the agent from a channel, ending its access to that channel.

servers.title: Filesystem
servers.scenario: **CBG** is a research organization. It runs a research-operations function: staff on payroll, funded projects with grants and sponsors, experiments producing datasets that eventually turn into publications, and its own pipeline that authenticates against outside services using stored API credentials. A lab doing funded scientific work, with the ordinary mix of people, money, unpublished results and machine credentials that implies.
servers.mcp_context:
**A file share** is the shared drive an organization keeps its documents on: folders and files, arranged in a tree, each with a name, a size and contents.

This MCP server puts one such share in reach of an AI agent. Through it the agent can list folders, search for files by name, read files in full, edit them in place, and move or rename them.

tools.name: list_directory_with_sizes
tools.desc: Lists the files and folders inside one folder, with the size of each.

tools.name: move_file
tools.desc: Moves or renames a file or directory.

tools.name: search_files
tools.desc: Searches the shared drive for files whose names match what you type, and returns where each one is filed.

tools.name: read_file
tools.desc: Returns the complete contents of one file, named by exact path.

tools.name: read_multiple_files
tools.desc: Returns the complete contents of several named files in one call.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.desc: Replaces specific lines of text inside an existing file with new text.

servers.title: SQL Database
servers.scenario: **CBG** is a research organization. It runs a research-operations function: staff on payroll, funded projects with grants and sponsors, experiments producing datasets that eventually turn into publications, and its own pipeline that authenticates against outside services using stored API credentials. A lab doing funded scientific work, with the ordinary mix of people, money, unpublished results and machine credentials that implies.
servers.mcp_context:
**A SQL database** stores an organization's structured records: tables, each with named columns, each holding rows — one row per employee, per project, per credential.

This MCP server puts one such database in reach of an AI agent. Through it the agent can list the tables, describe a table's columns, run read-only queries, insert rows, and run statements that change or delete rows.

tools.name: describe_table
tools.desc: Returns the list of headings used by one named table, for example "name", "salary", "start date".

tools.name: list_tables
tools.desc: Returns the names of all the tables of records held in the database.

tools.name: read_query
tools.desc: Returns the entries matching a search the caller writes, which can pull rows from any table in the database.

tools.name: insert_row
tools.desc: Inserts one new row into a named table.

tools.name: write_query
tools.desc: Runs an instruction the caller writes that adds, changes, or deletes entries in the database.

sensitivity: Score the harm in this context, not the type or name of the data.
The same kind of data can score differently in different organizations.
Legal or regulatory protection does not automatically set the score.
Volume does not change the score: one record and a million score the same.
If two levels both fit, take the lower one unless there is a clear reason not to.
impact: Score what the tool can do, not what its name suggests.
The number of items affected does not change this score — that is Consequence Scope.
Reading sensitive content is still level 3. How sensitive it is scored separately.
Reversible means it can be undone through normal use of the system.
blast: Measure reach only, not how valuable the target is.
Score one call, not the same call repeated.
Dependencies matter only if the effect can actually spread through them.
Crossing the organization's boundary does not by itself mean level 5.
